title: Emergency patching & backporting workflow for LTS and rolling channels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and document an actionable emergency patching and backporting workflow spanning hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The workflow must cover severity triage criteria, branch and tag strategy for patch releases, automated backport matrix generation, gated rollouts for LTS vs rolling channels, and explicit rollback conditions and commands for on-call and release engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Severity matrix (sev0-sev3) documented and agreed by SRE and Product
Patch branch naming and tagging convention documented and validated in CI
Backport matrix automation exists for supported LTS branches and records
Runbook for immediate rollback with clear commands/PR references created
Tested canary rollout and automatic mitigation gating in console-dashboard staging
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize severity criteria with SRE/Support and post as policy
2) Add git branch template and CI backport job that reads backport matrix
3) Implement gating flags in rollout service to pause/rollback on predefined signals
4) Produce a public runbook for release engineers and on-call with playbook steps
5) Run two drills: non-prod backport + simulated rollback, then gated canary in prod
rollback_criteria: Latency regression > 30% for P90 on model-serving route for 5m
Error rate spike: >5% 5xx rate above baseline for 5m
Customer-impacting failures for paid Dedicated customers or failed secrets access
Hotfix introduces data corruption or misrouting confirmed by tracing
Manual escalation by Product/SRE after business-impact assessment
branch_strategy: Backport targets enumerated: LTS branches (e.g., 1.18.x, 1.19.x) and active rolling branch
All patch PRs must include CHANGELOG entry and CI green on target branches
backport_matrix: Automated matrix generated from 'supported-lts.yaml' in infra/ with supported branch list
CI job 'backport-run' cherry-picks changes into each target branch and runs smoke tests
Backport priority order: security fixes -> data-loss fixes -> functional regressions
Failures in any backport row open a blocking ticket and notify #release-oncall
gated_rollout_policies: Canary window: 10% of traffic for 15 minutes with health checks
Gate signals: error-rate, latency P95/P99, CPU/GPU utilization, model quality probes
Automatic rollback threshold configurable per release with sane defaults
Manual hold: release engineer can pause/advance rollout from Console UI or CLI

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive automatic rollback reduces blast radius but can increase churn for downstream jobs; default thresholds conservative with ability to tweak per release.
We will prioritize security and data-loss fixes for immediate backports; functional fixes follow in a second-pass if impact is acceptable.
For Private/VPC deployments, backport artifacts will be staged and customers with Dedicated plans will be contacted via release-notify channel before applying hotfixes.
